question: What has keys but no locks, space but no rooms, and you can enter but cannot go inside?
What has hands but cannot clap?
What gets wetter the more it dries?
What has one eye but cannot see?
What has teeth but cannot bite?
What has a neck but no head?
What has legs but cannot walk?
What has ears but cannot hear?
What can run but never walks, has a mouth but never talks, has a head but never weeps, has a bed but never sleeps?
What goes up but never comes down?
What is full of holes but still holds water?
What has a face and two hands but no arms or legs?
What has four wheels and flies?
What building has the most stories?
What has a thumb and four fingers but is not alive?
I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. I have no body but come alive with the wind. What am I?
What has a tail and a head but no body?
What is always in front of you but cannot be seen?
What invention lets you look right through a wall?
I am light as a feather, but the strongest person cannot hold me for more than five minutes. What am I?
I have cities but no houses, forests but no trees, and water but no fish. What am I?
The more you take, the more you leave behind. What am I?
I have branches but no fruit, trunk but no bark, and leaves but no trees. What am I?
What can travel around the world while staying in the corner?
What comes once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a thousand years?
I am taken from a mine and shut up in a wooden case, from which I am never released, yet I am used by almost everyone. What am I?
What has a bottom at the top?
What can you catch but not throw?
What is so fragile that saying its name breaks it?
What can fill a room but takes up no space?
I have a spine but no bones. I have chapters but no lessons. What am I?
I go in dry and come out wet, the longer I am in, the stronger I get. What am I?
What has one head, one foot, and four legs?
What word is spelled the same forwards and backwards?
What can you hold without touching it?
I am always hungry and must always be fed. The finger I touch will soon turn red. What am I?
What gets shorter the more you use it?
What has many rings but no fingers?
What kind of room has no doors or windows?
I have a golden head, I have a golden tail, but I have no golden body. What am I?
What goes up when rain comes down?
What can you break without touching it?
I am not alive, but I grow. I do not have lungs, but I need air. I do not have a mouth, but water kills me. What am I?
What flies without wings?
What has a ring but no finger?
I shrink every time you use me. What am I?
What has an eye in the middle but cannot see?
I am the beginning of everything, the end of everywhere. I am the beginning of eternity, the end of time and space. What am I?
I have a thousand needles but I do not sew. What am I?
What walks on four legs in the morning, two legs at noon, and three legs in the evening?
The one who makes it sells it. The one who buys it never uses it. The one who uses it never knows they are using it. What is it?
I am the son of water, but when water rises I die. What am I?
A man looks at a painting and says, 'Brothers and sisters I have none, but that man's father is my father's son.' Who is in the painting?
What can be seen once in a minute, twice in a moment, but never in a hundred years?
I have lakes with no water, mountains with no stone, and cities with no buildings. What am I?
I am always there, some miles before you, slightly to one side or other of the road. I cannot be reached, even touched. What am I?
You throw away the outside and cook the inside. Then you eat the outside and throw away the inside. What did you eat?
What gets bigger the more you take away from it?
I have no body but I wear a coat. I have no legs but I leave footprints. I have no voice but I make sounds. What am I?
Two fathers and two sons went fishing. They caught three fish and each person had exactly one fish. How is this possible?
answer: There were only three people: a grandfather, his son, and his grandson.

question: The more of me there is, the less you see. What am I?
What has a wing but cannot fly?
What runs all day but never gets tired?
I have a bark but no bite. What am I?
What has a tongue but cannot taste?
What is always on your way but never in your way?
What has two legs but cannot walk without help?
What do you throw out when you need it and take in when you do not?
I am a fruit but also a color. What am I?
What can you catch in summer but not in winter?
What starts with T, ends with T, and has T in it?
What has twenty-six letters but only four syllables?
I keep you warm but I am not alive. You put me on but I am not clothes. What am I?
What has spots but is not a disease?
What goes around the house but never inside?
What stands up when lying down?
answer: A nail sticking out of the floor.

question: What has a head, a tail, but no body and no legs?
What grows up while growing down?
answer: A goose (or duckling) — it grows up as it grows its down feathers.

question: What can go up a chimney down but not down a chimney up?
What do you find at the end of a rainbow?
What has four corners but only one room?
I have no doors, no windows, but a room inside. What am I?
I am wet when I dry. What am I?
What has keys but opens no locks, with space but no room?
What gets sharper the more you use your brain?
I move without legs and leave a trail without feet. What am I?
The more you feed me, the more I grow, but give me water and I will die. What am I?
What always ends everything?
I have hands that wave but never say hello. What am I?
What runs but has no legs, roars but has no voice box?
I am not a mirror, yet I show your face. I am not water, yet I have waves. What am I?
What has four legs in the morning and in the evening, but only two at noon?
answer: A dog — puppies walk on all fours, adults walk on all fours too, but playfully the riddle mirrors the sphinx riddle flipped.

question: I have a single eye but I thread the world together. What am I?
What can you serve but never eat?
answer: A tennis ball (a serve in tennis).

question: What has a heart that does not beat?
I start tall and grow short the older I get. What am I?
What can you hold in your left hand but not your right?
What kind of coat can be put on only when wet?
I have a head like a cat, feet like a cat, and a tail like a cat, but I am not a cat. What am I?
What loses its head every morning and gets it back every night?
What is black when you buy it, red when you use it, and grey when you throw it away?
What goes through a door but never goes in or comes out?
I can be cracked, played, and told, but I am not a joke. What am I?
What word has five letters but sounds like only one?
What comes down but never goes up?
The more you remove from me, the bigger I become. What am I?
I have no wings but I fly. I have no eyes but I cry. What am I?
What is seen in the middle of March and April, but cannot be seen at the beginning or end of either?
I belong to you but others use me more. What am I?
I have no life but I can die. What am I?
What comes once in a year, twice in a week, but never in a day?
I have all the knowledge you have but I am too small to hold even half your thoughts. What am I?
answer: Your brain (the paradox: your brain stores your knowledge yet cannot fully comprehend itself).

question: What can travel faster than the speed of light, yet has no mass and carries no energy?
I am a word. I become longer when you add a letter to make me shorter. What am I?
A cowboy rides into town on Friday, stays three days, and rides out on Friday. How?
What can you put in a barrel to make it lighter?
I have a head and a tail, but no body. Every time you use me, you lose a little of me. What am I?
I am always running but I have no legs. I am always thirsty but I have no mouth. What am I?
What is so delicate that even naming it breaks it?
I have no mouth yet I tell stories. I have no memory yet I remember everything. What am I?
What disappears the moment you say its name?
What is always behind you but can never be caught?
